title: Author’s closing note
html:
Hello, I'm Sing Shong.

At last, Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint has reached its conclusion after 2 years and 1 month of serialization.

As I carefully read every comment you left on installment 535, I began to get some idea of what you wanted to know (Reading each of your thoughtful comments made me very happy. I'm sorry that limited space prevents me from answering every question).

In this afterword, I'll focus on answering the questions that came up most often among the many you sent.

Q. Who are you, Author-nim?

I'm someone called Sing Shong.

Despite the announcements I've made about this time and again, I've heard all sorts of rumors about myself from various sources. Gender, occupation, age, and even imaginative backstories I could never have dreamed up······ In truth, I didn't think who Sing Shong was mattered very much. I'm only an intermediary setting down the characters of 『Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint』. That was why I wanted to leave the story of its author, Sing Shong, untold to the end. I also worried that if I revealed who I was, sentences that should exist for the characters would be read in entirely unintended ways because of the person called ‘Sing Shong’ (I've already heard things like that).

『Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint』 wasn't written because of Sing Shong's gender, age, or identity. Some writing may depend on particular circumstances, but 『Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint』, at least, isn't that sort of work. Even so, many people are still discussing these things. After much thought, I've decided to answer the question. If I'm going to be misunderstood anyway, I thought it would be better to speak openly and get it off my chest.

The ‘Sing Shong’ who set down 『Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint』 isn't one person.

This isn't a joke or a metaphor. Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint was written together by two people of different genders and ages—a married couple, to be precise.

The rumors circulating about us were very bewildering.

That was because whenever we visited Munpia, signed a contract for a work, or met people about cross-media projects (OSMU), ‘Sing’ and ‘Shong’ were always together (there was just one occasion when only one of us visited Munpia because of our schedules. I do wonder whether that was where the misunderstanding began).

There are things we're afraid of as we reveal this today. The moment we make it public, some people will take 『Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint』 apart and decide that ‘Sing’ wrote this bit and ‘Shong’ wrote that bit. But······ you won't find it easy to tell. We get mixed up ourselves.

Q. What led you to come up with Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint?

It was the summer of 2017. After finishing 『The World After the Fall』, Sing fell into a fairly long slump. The last bastion, the epic saga of Lee Hakhyun, warrior of literary fiction—『How to Become a Star Writer』—had flopped (the series is on hiatus; don't read it). Burned out for a while, Sing had no idea what to write. Every day was spent sprawled on the squishy floor. A sorry sight.

Then one day, Shong suddenly lifted their head and said something.

Shong : With the reader... let's move forward.

Sing : ?

Shong sprang up, suddenly went over to Sing's laptop, and started tapping away at the keyboard. The three lines that came of it.

「Kim Dokja (金獨子). My father gave me that name so I would become a man who was strong even on his own. But thanks to the name my father gave me, all I've become is an ordinary, lonely, single man.」

Shong : (pointing at the monitor) Keep writing from here.

Sing : I can't······.

Shong : You can!

Sing grumbled for a long while, but eventually wrote what came before and after those lines. And at that very instant. With a feeling as though something had struck the back of their head, a new universe opened up in their mind, and by the time they came to, the prologue and installment 1 were finished in a flash······ It would be great fun to gloss over the rest with a story like that, but leaving the explanation there would do a disservice to the character who let us tell this story.

In fact, the theme of 『Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint』 was something Sing had been thinking about for 8 years.

‘A story about stories.’ ‘A web novel about web novels.’ ‘Genre fiction about genre fiction.’ I'd wanted to write about this for a very long time, and had experimented with these themes in earlier work as well.

Through several failures, I studied what form would convey the theme effectively. Rough as it is, this is the result.

For all my shortcomings, I was able to come this far thanks to the characters, and to the warm eyes that watched over them.

Q. Do you have plans for your next work?

None for the time being.

Q. Will there be a guide to the setting of Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint?

We haven't discussed it with our management yet, but I'll try to make it happen if possible.

Q. Are there plans for Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint merchandise?

As far as I know, our management is preparing it.

Q. Do you plan to release print books, collector's editions, or hardcovers?

Yes. Print books and hardcovers are planned.

Q. Do you have plans for side stories?

Yes. They'll probably be written alongside our work on the print edition. We'll let you know when a date is set.

Q. Have you considered a webtoon adaptation?

The webtoon of 『Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint』 is currently in production. Excellent creators from an amazing team are handling it, so we're very excited too. We expect it to launch in the first half of this year.

Q. Is a screen adaptation underway?

Some of you may already know this, but 『Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint』 currently has a contract for 5 films with the production company Realies Pictures. Alongside the Korean film adaptation, we're also talking with overseas production companies about long-form television dramas and other projects, so it seems we'll be able to share good news on that front soon as well.

Q. Which part did you most enjoy writing during the long serialization?

Sing : Personally, I most enjoyed ‘The 73rd Demon King’ and ‘The Oldest Dream’. I'd thought about both for so long that I could write them in one go without agonizing over them. I also really enjoyed writing ‘King of a Kingless World’.

Shong : The story I was writing at the time was always the one I enjoyed most. Right now, I suppose the epilogue stands out most in my memory. I'd also been waiting a long time for that part, and I think that made working on it all the more enjoyable.

Q. Which character do you think is most like you?

Sing : Actually, I don't think any of them are like me. But I know who Shong is like. In a lot of ways, Shong resembles Han Sooyoung. I'm sure the answer below will sound just like her, too.

Shong : I'm a little like every character, and unlike them too. I'm embarrassed to say who I resemble, so to change the subject, Sing resembles Gilyoung. Gilyoung is an innocent, stubborn child. I think that's how he'd have grown up if he'd loved stories instead of bugs.

Q. Which character is your favorite, or the one you're most attached to?

Sing : Of course I like them all... but personally, I think I'm especially attached to Han Sooyoung and Jung Heewon. Heewon, in particular, keeps weighing on my mind. If I get the chance, I'd like to tell more of her story.

Shong : I like Hayoung. I just do. I wanted to let Hayoung speak and act better, but I'm left with a lot of regrets. And I'm not sure whether this counts as a character, but I really like dumpling Joonghyuk too.

Q. What do you most want to do once Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint is finished?

Sing : I've spent such a long time thinking about this day, but now that it's here, I feel strange. It really seemed as though there were still plenty of stories to set down, but oddly enough, right now I don't seem to have a sentence to add to the characters' lives. Even when I close my eyes, I don't feel anyone hitting the back of my head. It's strange, so very strange, and I think I'll spend a while steeped in that feeling.

Shong : I'm sure there were all sorts of things I wanted to do, but now that I've finished, I find myself thinking that this was what I wanted to do most of all. Thinking about it a little more, I don't want to be involved in anything at all for a while. I think that might be all right for at least a week or so.

Q. You called <WATF> ‘a novel about a naked man thrusting’. How would you describe <ORV>?

Sing : A story less harmful than WATF.

Shong : A story in which someone liked someone, and the whole world became better for it.

Q. Did you ever fall into a slump while serializing ORV? If so, how did you get through it?

Sing : I don't think there was ever a time when I wasn't in a slump. Every day meant overcoming it, and failing for even a day meant falling apart. I just gritted my teeth and held on. If I didn't write, the story would stop. I'm glad I was able to write it to the end.

Shong : Sing's slump was my slump. If Sing couldn't write a draft, there was nothing I could do either. While Sing was sunk in despair, I think I tried to keep my head above that swamp as much as possible and find something I could do right away. When I sank into despair, Sing carried me on their back through the swamp. I think we both tried our best to avoid ever reaching a moment when we did nothing.

Q. Is there anything you'd like to say in closing?

I read each question you sent with gratitude. There were so many interesting questions, but wherever possible, I left out those about the work itself. I'm very sorry. I felt that answering them here would diminish the meaning of the sentences those friends devoted their lives to writing. I hope I'll have space to answer those questions in writing again someday.

So many people helped us reach this point.

CEO Kim Hwanchul, whose generous advice always gave us strength. Director Lee Kyungsoo, who threw himself into opening new possibilities for ORV. Editor Kim Taehyun and our contact Lim Joori, who always looked after every detail, including matters beyond the serialization.

Mr. J, who kept the outside winds at bay for us while we were ill. Author Ir, who was our courage, right by our side.

The four cover artists who crafted wonderful faces for our children.

Every character in 『Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint』, for granting us a story beyond anything we deserved.

The people we love, whose names we dare not write for fear of causing them trouble.

And finally, each of you—the one reader who shared in reading their stories and breathed probability into them.

We're not dead yet and are writing this sentence thanks to the sentences you gave us. If one day we can write another sentence, that too will be because of the sentences you gave us.

Thank you for staying with 『Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint』 all the way to the end.

February 3, 2020. Sincerely, Sing Shong.
